Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires and the players walk out to take the field as Sri Lanka Women come out to chase the highest total of this tournament. Chamari Athapaththu and Vishmi Gunarathne are the two opening batters for Sri Lanka Women. Renuka Singh Thakur to start the attack for India Women. Let's play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka’s bowlers toiled hard but were unable to stop India’s onslaught, especially in the latter stages of the innings. With a target of 173 to chase, Sri Lanka will have a tough task ahead of them. India’s bowlers will now be looking to back up their batters and secure a comprehensive victory. Stay tuned as Sri Lanka begins their chase shortly.

Despite the twin blows, India kept up the pressure with Jemimah Rodrigues chipping in with a quickfire 16 off just 10 balls, keeping the scoreboard ticking. The final phase of India’s innings, however, was all about their captain, Harmanpreet Kaur. Coming in with the score at 100/2, Harmanpreet paced her innings perfectly, delivering some crucial hits in the death overs. She provided the much-needed acceleration, finding the boundary regularly and finishing the innings with back-to-back fours. The Indian skipper brought up her half-century in just 27 balls, leading India to a formidable total.

However, the left-handed Mandhana broke her shackles in the final over of the powerplay, smashing a boundary over the bowler’s head and hitting India’s first six of the tournament. This brought momentum to India’s innings as both batters started finding the gaps and increasing the run rate. Mandhana, showing her class, brought up her 27th T20I fifty off 36 balls, as the partnership between her and Shafali neared the 100-run mark.

India Women put on a dominant batting display, posting an imposing total of 172/3 in their 20 overs, marking the highest team score in this year's World Cup. After opting to bat first, the opening duo of Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana provided a solid platform for the Women in Blue. Though they began cautiously, focusing on strike rotation in the early overs, Shafali quickly found her rhythm, while Mandhana initially struggled to find her timing.

FOUR! India Women have announced their arrival at the ICC Women's World Cup, 2024. Is it a bit too late? Only time will tell. Pitched up around middle and off, Harmanpreet Kaur clears her front leg and muscles this past a diving mid off fielder for a boundary to close the innings. India Women posts 172 on board. India Women now need to restrict Sri Lanka Women to around 130 to have a better NRR than the White Ferns.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all in readiness for this crucial game to begin. The umpires are out in the middle followed by the players of Sri Lanka Women led by Chamari Athapaththu. For India Women, it's the dynamic duo of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma right at the top. The duo is yet to provide a decent start to India Women in this tournament. Sri Lanka Women will start their bowling attack with the spin of Inoshi Fernando. A match-up for Verma but will she take Inoshi on? Let's find out.
Time for the National Anthems of the respective countries. It will be Sri Lanka's first followed by the National Anthem of India.

PITCH REPORT! Ian Bishop notes that conditions at the Dubai International Stadium are cooler compared to the earlier game, which is pleasant for the players as the day turns into night. Discussing the dimensions, he mentions that the boundary to the right from the Sports City end is 57 meters, a short side, while the left is larger at 63 meters, with 73 meters straight down the ground. WV Raman adds that the surface has been drier, favoring spinners, but during the evening, the ball tends to skid on better, making it more favorable for batters to play shots.

Sri Lanka Women's captain Chamari Athapaththu says she feels the conditions are slow and low but believes her team is sticking to their plans and hopes to play their best cricket. She emphasizes the need to be fearless in the middle overs, noting that while big shots are possible during the powerplay, the focus should shift to rotating the strike afterward. Athapaththu also confirms one change in the lineup, with Hasini Perera missing out and Ama Kanchana coming into the side.

The skipper of India, Harmanpreet Kaur, says they are going to bat first and so far they have not done well but will be looking to put a big total on board. Mentions that they are really happy that they get support despite of the venue where they play. Reckons that they played good cricket in the Asia Cup as well but just had one bad day and Sri Lanka Women took advantage of that but it's a new game today and they will look to start afresh. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

This match is pivotal for both sides as they fight for survival in the tournament. Sri Lanka Women are battling to stay alive, and India Women need to make no errors to secure a semi-final berth. As the two teams prepare for this high-stakes clash, all eyes will be on the batters who hold the key to unlocking victory. Stay tuned as we bring you all the pre-match excitement and the toss.

India Women, coming off a tough defeat to New Zealand, also cannot afford any slip-ups. With a semi-final spot on the line, the pressure is mounting, especially with uncertainties surrounding captain Harmanpreet Kaur. After suffering a neck injury during her innings against Pakistan, where she retired hurt at 29, her participation in the match against Sri Lanka Women remains doubtful. The Indian batting order, already under strain with their openers struggling at the top as the Indian vice-captain Smriti Mandhana has not found her feet yet in the tournament, will need middle-order batters like Jemimah Rodrigues, Deepti Sharma, and Richa Ghosh to step up and share the responsibility, especially if their skipper is unable to take the field.

Sri Lanka Women, who emerged victorious when these two rivals last met in the Asia Cup final in July, will be looking to replicate that success to keep their tournament hopes alive. With two losses to Pakistan and Australia already in their campaign, Sri Lanka Women now face a must-win scenario, needing victories in both of their remaining matches to have a shot at the knockout stages.

This encounter carries significant weight for both teams as they vie for a spot in the semi-finals.

The much-anticipated clash is set for the 2024 ICC Women's T20 World Cup as the Asian champions, Sri Lanka Women, take on one of the tournament's top contenders, India Women. This match is a repeat of the 2024 Women's Asia Cup final, but things have not been smooth for Sri Lanka Women in this World Cup so far. They’ve suffered two crushing defeats, and now their hopes of progressing further hang by a thread. Sri Lanka Women’s struggles have stemmed from their shaky batting lineup. Heavily reliant on their captain Chamari Athapaththu, the team desperately needs her to produce a captain’s knock. Young opener Vishmi Gunarathne and middle-order star Harshitha Samarawickrama, who was the hero in the Asia Cup, also carry the burden of Sri Lanka’s hopes. Players like Nilakshika Silva and Hasini Perera have shown promise, but they must step up when it counts most. On the bowling front, Sri Lanka has been more solid. Udeshika Prabodani leads the pace attack with four wickets to her name, while Sugandika Kumari’s accurate spin has been a bright spot. Chamari can also contribute with the ball, and Inoka Ranaweera plays a crucial supporting role. This is a must-win game for Sri Lanka Women if they want to stay alive in the tournament. India Women, on the other hand, come into this match with mixed fortunes. After a demoralizing loss to New Zealand, they bounced back strongly, claiming victory in the heated contest against arch-rivals Pakistan. However, the injury cloud over captain Harmanpreet Kaur casts doubt over their momentum. If Kaur is unavailable, it could be a huge blow to India's chances. Smriti Mandhana, who has yet to fire, must take charge at the top, while Shafali Verma got her touch back with a decent knock in the last game. Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh add firepower in the middle. Deepti Sharma, one of the top all-rounders, will also play a key role with both bat and ball. Their spinners - Asha Sobhana and Shreyanka Patil are crucial on these UAE pitches that favor turn. The stakes are high for both teams. Sri Lanka Women must rediscover their form from the Asia Cup, while India Women looks to build on their momentum. Will Sri Lanka pull off another famous victory? Or will India march closer to the knockout stage? We’re about to find out in this high-octane battle!
